text_fidelity_a:
Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge Games- Tiny Hands Challenge Children's Toy has all the things that make for a great game- it’s challenging, fun, moves fast and has plenty of hilarious laughter. The game comes with: 2 tiny hands, 2 tinier hands, 3 sets of activity cards (151 total), 20 scoring tokens, 1 spinner, 1 string (shoe lace), 1 ball, 1 sand timer (time is one minute), 1 wager mat and instructions. You can play with 4-10 players and recommended age is 8 and up.

You begin by dividing into 2 teams- yellow and blue. You set up the wager mat and the 3 decks of cards. Then set out the hands, spinner, string, ball and sand timer. You play rock, paper, scissors to see who goes first. You spin the spinner to see which activity card you will do and which hands you will do it with- tiny or tinier. Some of the activities use pens, paper, cups and coins, so you will want to have these items available too.

Once you know what activity you must do with which hands, you make a wager. If you lose, your opponent gets the token points. Even if you win, your opponent can challenge you. The 3 sets of cards are: Solo, Pair and Charades. The timer being one minute long makes the challenges and charades almost impossible to finish in such a short time. Luckily, some of the challenges don’t use the timer and give you multiple tries. There is also a Face Off, where both teams do a challenge at the same time. Doing the challenges and charades in such a short time with these tiny hands is almost impossible and laughing so hard totally impossible. The first team to collect 31 token points wins. Great Fun, Challenges and Laughter. 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge

Fisher-Price Julius Jr. Rock 'n Playhouse Box Fisher Price knew what they were doing when they designed this Julius Jr. Rock'n Playhouse Box for ages 2 and up. The littlest children ages 2 and 3 years old just love it. The children really enjoy having Julius Jr. skateboard down the ramp and slide down the circular slide after going through a pie-shaped door.

They also love having Julius Jr. look through the telescope up on the rooftop and slide on the conveyor belt opening up the double doors where a Martian is ready for take-off in his space craft. But, their favorite thing is seeing the colorful dance floor light up and play music when Julius steps on it, as well as riding the elevator. There is even a disco ball attached to a weather vane upstairs that spins.

The elevator moves up to the second floor and rooftop, and with every floor, you hear Julius Jr. speak. He says things like, when he is looking out the window, What a beautiful day, I'm gonna need my sun hat. There are many sayings you will hear every time a bell rings at the floor stops, and they are different at times, so you will never know exactly what will be said.

This simple Playhouse is colorful and the pieces are made for little hands- easy to handle and nothing sharp. The Playhouse requires 2 AA batteries, which are included. You can also purchase extra Figure Packs, and you will want to, as Julius Jr. will have much more fun with a friend or two. Fisher Price has also made 2 more Playsets for Julius Jr. to play in- a Sortin' Sagebrush Farm and a Twirl-A-World Amusement Park. These sets will attach to this Playhouse making a world for Julius Jr. and your child to play in.

This 4 Star Rock'n Playhouse Box is a very simple set geared for the very young to enjoy with it's bright colors, sturdiness and simple moving parts. Two and three year olds especially love it.

text_fidelity_a: Doggie Doo Corgi Game - Unpredictable Action - Feed The Doggie and Collect His Doo to Win - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This type of thing isn't usually my cup of tea and I typically dislike potty humor. This looked like something to bring humor on the days that my guys aren't getting along, though. It is on the weird side(even thought so from my 3 boys), with all the noises, but it is also on the humorous side. To play, you stick a bit of slime("food") into the bone. The players take turns rolling the die and squeezing the bone the amount rolled. Each player has a shovel that they place behind the dog to catch the "doos" before squeezing the bone. Each time the dog poos, you have to refill the bone. Once all the slime is gone, the player with the most "doos" wins. Had I known that the game used slime, I never would have gotten it. I've had to throw out too many items ruined from it to want it in my home anymore. We just try to be extra careful when playing. It comes with two bags, but it only takes one to play. The second bag is for if the first gets ruined. It says on the bag that it's non-toxic, but to still wash hands after touching it. When the game works, it's fun and makes us laugh. We've had lots of trouble getting it to work properly, though. Many times it won't seal just right(I guess) and no amount of squeezing the bone will make anything happen. It warns not to put too much, which we've tried not to do, and to also make sure the bone is pushed all the way in, which we've tried to do. It still won't work for us half the time, though, which makes it frustrating. If the slime ever gets stuck, the game does come with a stick to push it out. It also comes with a puzzle, which is a nice bonus. Overall, it's still a fun game.

Matchbox Cars Playset, 4-Level Toy Garage & Tow Truck in 1:64 Scale, Kid-Powered Elevator, Car Repair Station & Spiral Ramp For my 4 and a half year old grandson. He loves his cars and so this was a nice compact "repair garage" play structure. It will not be something you will want to break down daily and store, it will need to be up and available for immediate play. It will stay at my house for his visits and be stored on a closet shelf between visits. It came with one little tow truck vehicle. There is no car storage; this is just a play activity. A turning knob on top of the elevator brings cars up to individual floor levels and there are gates on the ramps that divert the cars to a car maintenance floor and a car wash floor in the structure. Although it says it's 4 level, there is nothing but a ramp from the elevator on the upper level and the lower level is really just the entry to the elevator and an open accessible area underneath that the imagination can invent a use for.

The instructions were also less than stellar and being only in black and white, identifying some of the little pieces was sometimes guesswork. There are small pieces that can be pulled off, so observe the recommended age group for this toy. We were not interested in all the many decorative stickers that can be applied on this toy, so only used what we wanted to.

It appears to be sturdy enough and, if incorporated with some other play structures, could keep his attention for a lengthy period of play time.

Thomas & Friends TrackMaster, Castle Quest Set You just can't go wrong with a train set for children! With 3 little boys, trains are extra special in our house.

Thankfully, my husband put this train set together. The first time takes awhile since you're learning the pieces. You WILL need the instructions, or at least the picture to look at. Make sure you don't immediately throw everything away. Putting it together gets easier and easier each time. If your little ones are like mine, they will feel the need to take it apart time and time again. :) Otherwise, the set up is super simple.

The train itself stays on the track very well, but once we hooked the wagon part on the back, we couldn't seem to keep it on the track. It kept running off. That's my only complaint with this set. We don't *need* the wagon to enjoy, though. Of course, if you're actually playing with the crown, you will, but the crown got misplaced pretty quickly at our house. Those small extra pieces really don't stand a chance at our house most the time.

Overall, this is a train set that we really enjoy, and recommend! It's the second of the "Thomas" sets that we've added to our collection. We like them!

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs We've been making potholders at home and it seemed like we were always running out of the colors we wanted, so we ordered replacements from several different sources to see what worked best. Although these are not the easiest to use, they by far make the best finished product. This is a great big bag of loops with very vibrant colors. The colors are great -- teal, cobalt, lime green, kelly green, pink, red, reddish-purple, yellow, orange -- enough to make some beautiful combinations. Compared to the other loops we've used, these are very thick and less stretchy. Because they are bulkier, they are a little harder to work with. I haven't found any that don't fit, though. On the flip side, the finished potholder is larger and holds its shape better. I've found that the stretchier brands seem to have a lot of nylon, and it doesn't seem like they'd hold up as well to hot dishes. These loops are kind of scraggly, with loose threads hanging off of them, but when you weave them together the loose threads aren't really a problem.

Someone commented that her daughter wasn't able to weave the edges with these because they were less stretchy. My daughter hasn't been able to weave the edges with these either, but she's very, very proud of the finished product as it is larger, more vibrant, and more even in shape than the potholders made with the stretchier loops.

If you want something that's really easy to use, you might check for the loops made by klutz or others, as these might not be the best bet. If you want to make cool potholders, though, these are a good choice.

UPDATE: I'm back a year later to buy more. Glad that I was able to find the good loops again. And now that my daughter is 8, she no longer has difficulty weaving the edges -- most of the time. Also, these are much easier to weave off the edges when you use the metal loom, rather than the plastic ones.

UPDATE #2: Almost two years later, and my daughter is back making potholders, this time trying to create her own designs. Need more loops!
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs

Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended I'm not quite the telescope connoisseur, though I'm quite well versed in optics (avid photographer), and I've discovered there's a bit of a gulf between the "wouldn't it be nice to have a telescope" and those sold to diehard astronomers. This one falls into the former category, and as such I"m not really comparing this to higher end models.

In the lower end realm, I still expect clear optics, no noticeable optical defects, and a stable base. This one checks those boxes. The optics look clean and clear to the naked eye, though lab testing would show where higher end models excel, and it's not the brightest lens (all lenses lose some light due to transmission loss in lens materials and dispersal), but it met my expectations. The tripod is well built enough for this model telescope, but it's no remarkable. As it's geared towards budding astronomers, especially youngsters, the included guide and list of projects to get you going is definitely a strength.

4 stars due to no faults of it's own, though it's not that remarkable either. Recommended, though may want to consider other models.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended

text_fidelity_a:
Micro Arcade Qbert I've bought almost all of this company's whole Tiny Arcade series, and have really liked them. The games are dumbed down and reprogrammed for the tiny screen - MAME emulation, they ain't. But generally they get the basic feel of the games right and are great fun to play.

These are really, really bad ports. I've played a lot of bad Atari ports in my day, but these are some of the worst. Super Breakout is incredibly slow and the ball behaves ridiculously. Asteroids is destroyed by the fact that the titular asteroids do not follow any kind of physics whatsoever - after you blow one up, the chunks shoot in every direction.

I also have the Series 1, which has the cream of the kinda rotten crop, Missile Command. Missile Command is full of bugs - it just randomly spams the "OUT" and "LOW" indicators any old place on screen, totally at random. It's hilariously nerfed - I survived many rounds with my missile batteries destroyed because the Russkies just couldn't seem to aim at anything they didn't already level. Missiles explode immediately and the explosion fades away almost instantly, completely ruining the strategy of the game. And yet, though it's a lame version of the legitimate game, it's nevertheless a curiously addicting game in its own right.

Centipede comes off very badly. The game does not work well with the control scheme, and the bubble buttons are an even worse replacement for the trackball than normal d-pads. Everything is off kilter and badly tuned - the centipede will be at the bottom row in a matter of seconds. I thought this was the least fun of the four "main" games.

The bonus game is Pong. Pong is Pong, kind of, sans the paddle controller. It frankly disappoints me about myself that I still have so much fun with it.

That said, these are still kind of fun, in the way the old Tiger LCD handhelds could be. They're really far from the originals, but in a pinch, they're nice to have around.

The build quality is bizarrely misweighted. The bubble-switch buttons have really firm resistance, but I kinda like them. They have a sound on/off swith that is sorely missed in the Tiny Arcade units, and the feeling of the back of the unit is great, but the actual screen area picks up scratches like it was made of butter. I got an Amazon Warehouse Deals used one, and had to send it back because the screen was just unusable.

So, as long as you don't put them in your pocket with your car keys, and as long as you have a lot of tolerance for cheap handheld jankiness, it might be worth your pennies. But buyer beware - a LOT of tolerance is required.
text_fidelity_b: Micro Arcade Qbert

Scrabble Turbo Slam My feelings about this product are mixed -- We've long been fans of Scrabble, and thought we'd shake things up a bit by trying a different variation of the game. The Electronic Turbo Slam device, first required (3)- AAA batteries (not included). The device, when slammed has pretty loud sound effects/music, which I found annoying after a short while. I also thought there was too much commotion for me with everyone trying to slap down cards to change the letters, and I wasn't crazy about making just (4) letter words. As an adult, baby boomer, I much prefer the standard game of Scrabble -- quiet, relaxed and educational, and with more word potential.

I can see that this would be a great game for parents to play with young children to help them get interested in learning new words -- I would use it as an educational tool, instead of having them feel pressured to make words at record speed.

On the other hand, the speed and noise factor, would probably appeal to lots of teens. Overall, the game is relatively inexpensive, and worth a try for families who enjoy word faster paced, action filled games.

Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity My grandson is almost three years old, and I thought he’d enjoy this toy...that was until I received it. Upon first inspection you notice a cheaply made zip-up half circle that opens to expose rivets that a child is supposed to insert the enclosed plastic big “buttons”. Let me just tell you that there’s no way that my grandson can attach these things to the mat - it took all my strength and dexterity to get one or two to pop in place. This is simply too difficult for a child of any age and not challenging but frustrating. Then there’s these cute little ocean-themed felt cut-outs that you’re supposed to “hook” around the installed buttons. They’re brightly colored and my grandson did enjoy taking them off and on the buttons for about 15 minutes. Then there’s a few pieces of string...some are about 4” long (too short to practice tying and really too short for a toddler to attempt to thread through four holes on the felt pieces) and others are about 6” long. ALSO, Within fifteen minutes of play my toddler was pulling on the buttons attempting to remove them and the rivets we’re poppong off and the mat was falling apart, not to mention the tiny metal circles all over the floor were now a choking hazard and the mat no longer works in the holes that lost the rivets.

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity

Mattel Games Pictionary Air Harry Potter Family Game for Kids & Adults with Light Wand & Themed Picture Clue Cards This is a good game that you can play with the kids, and the play will be relatively competitive. The kids have a significant advantage in terms of ease of cards - they come with simple words, and a pre-done drawing to help out the littlest of the littles. Adults have conceptual items rather than specific nouns, which is certainly a challenge.

The technology of the pen, though, is what is going to make or break this game. It works pretty well, but is not infalliable. Kids love to watch the image appear as they draw in mid air and see the image appear on a screen, and the adults we played with certainly enjoyed watching their images appear...incorrectly. It's very challenging. We didn't have any glitches in playing the game, but we did have a bunch of very odd images appearing.

This is a fun gag, and a good addition to your family game collection.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary Air Harry Potter Family Game for Kids & Adults with Light Wand & Themed Picture Clue Cards

text_fidelity_a:
Westcott 6" Titanium Precision Scissors - Violet I’m a crafter and a super office supply freak. I confess this so you will understand that I have a LOT of scissors. It is a well known fact that you need different scissors for different types of project. It’s also fact that there is something slightly wrong with every pair. It’s one of those mysteries like when you put a pair of socks in the dryer only one comes out. Head scratcher.
Against all odds, and the rules of the crafting universe, these scissors are perfect.
The handle is big enough for any size fingers. The grip is so comfortable I have not had a case of the “scissor cramps” no matter how long I use them for.
The blades are super sharp, aaaaallll the way down to the tips. They allow me to snip into the most minute 'V' of a paper cut out. Even better they let me cut the most clean appliqués for quilting. No need to tear out that last little bit of paper you couldn’t get with your scissors. I’m so used to doing that it now feels like I’m missing a step. They cut cleanly through even my thickest macrame cord, which is why I bought them in the first place.
The anti-stick is no joke. These are now my exclusive washi tape cutting scissors. I don’t need to get out the rubbing alcohol or Goof-Off to wipe down the blades to get the adhesive off. It simply doesn’t stick to the blades at all. It’s a miracle!
When I was first looking at these to buy them I giggled a bit about the lanyard, like who would use that? The answer is me! I use the lanyard! Most of the time I have them hanging right next to my workspace where I can grab them easy peasy. But I find myself putting it around my neck when I’m moving around. It keeps the sharp point safe and they don’t get lost under the inevitable mess I make. And when I’m working on a large macrame project I don’t need to drop the cord to get the scissors.
Now don’t shake your head, I haven’t lost my mind entirely, I don’t use them for tape/paper AND fabric. That would be up there with drinking orange juice then brushing my teeth. No, instead I simply bought two pairs. The orange/grey for fabric and the purple/pink for everything else. I probably could’ve used the same pair but why upset the balance of the universe, amma right?
Will these replace all of your scissors? Nope. But they for sure will replace all your smaller pairs. I definitely recommend getting these, in all available colors!
text_fidelity_b: Westcott 6" Titanium Precision Scissors - Violet

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+ We are really loving these Hot Dots learning activity books. My preschooler loves to count, so this math book is great for getting some counting practice in. I never worked on pattern recognition, and this book includes that, so I’m so glad we’re getting some exposure with that (i.e. circle, circle, square, circle, circle —insert what comes next). It also covers big and small, shapes, the most and the least themes, heavy and light, as well as matching. There’s a lot to learn in this workbook, and it’s a lot of fun.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Math - Preschool Math Workbook to Learn Counting & Colors with Interactive Activities, Classroom Essentials, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Kanagawa Game Kanagawa is a board game about making the most cohesive panorama painting.

The first thing you'll notice about Kanagawa is that it has tremendous components. The little paintbrush bits are unique and well-made, and the way that the cards fit together is really cool. The art and graphic design make it easy for players to figure out how to play, and even the board is well-designed.

Unfortunately, gameplay is pretty basic. Each turn, new cards will be put on the board, either face up or face down depending on the positioning. Players can then either take some of the cards, or allow more to come out, opening up the opportunity to their opponents to take the "best" cards. You then place these cards in panorama fashion on your piece of art, or you can use them as "skill" cards to allow you to paint more interesting paintings on later turns. There are bonus cards, and opportunities to gather more items, but that's really about it.

Aside from the excellent artwork, the only other good thing about this game is that you can explain the rules in only a few minutes. Decisions that you make along the way really are not all that important along the way. You can collect a lot of abilities along the way that you never get the opportunity to use, or you can find that you'd rather not use them because there are better moves for you. Overall, this game was pretty fast, easy to learn, but felt like your decisions were pretty arbitrary, and didn't matter in the end.
text_fidelity_b: Kanagawa Game

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends MINIS playset with 3 action-Packed stunt tracks! Great toy. Easy to assemble and good quality. Instructions are easy to follow. Took me about 15 mins. Does not come with batteries.

Pros:
1) easy assembly
2) holds out son’s attention span for about 30 mins
3) light weight and easy handling by toddler
4) easy storage- doesn’t take up a lot of room
5) 3 different race tracks with inter changeable track section
6) easy system to understand for a 2.5 year old

Cons (1 star deduction):
1) design flaws: if child feeds too many minis into the track it tends to creat a jam at the starting point and stop the track (easy fix: remove the minis)
2) design flaw: it also knocks off the minis if jammed
3) the interchangeably track part tends to create a jam if not lined up exactly and one has to be quick. A child might not have enough agility to be quick changing the track creating a jam if too many minis on the track.

No toy is perfect. With that said our son loves it and even we enjoy playing with it. That is all that counts and seeing the joy on his face is all this needs. It so worth purchasing this.

We use the mini as rewards system for our son’s potty training. He enjoys playing with them so much that we decided to get him the track before Christmas 🎄

text_fidelity_a:
KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+ It really is all it's cracked up to be! I have been eyeing it for almost two years and I got lucky and found it in November for $120. I waited to put it together until the night Santa stopped by our house. It did take a few hours to assemble but my husband never left his recliner. I only needed an extra set of hands once or twice and my mom easily did the job.

The top is tricky to attach because the freezer and microwave doors have a tendency to want to leap off the kitchen. I definitely recommend assembling on carpet--the freezer door fell off while I were attaching the top (it's totally stable after the top is attached) and my hardwood floors dinged the corner when the door landed.

If I had to put the kitchen together again, I would definitely get an Allen wrench drill-bit for my drill. The two types of Allen screws in the box have the same head so you can take one of them to the hardware store to ensure the proper drill bit fit. Using a low-power drill makes furniture assembly fast and SO much more pleasant. :)

My son loves it!!! He was only 18 months at Christmas so I was worried he wouldn't know what to do with a kitchen. To my surprise, he ran right to the stove and started turning knobs. He tested the sink handles to make sure they turned and then he started cooking! I totally recommend the utensils and stainless pots & pans from Ikea (they fit the burners perfect). The Melissa & Doug wooden pantry and fridge foods are awesome, as well. Very, very cute.

All-in-all, I am completely delighted with the quality and playtime potential this kitchen offers. My baby might not have any idea what I am talking about when we play "Iron Chef", but he knows how to stir, flip, move things to the sink and move food from the fridge to the microwave to the oven...

Oh, also, my big little guy is 33" already and he has to stand on his tip-toes to see inside his stock pot. He will be cooking for many years to come.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+

daughter was small, to now, with our little nieces and nephews. We got this Friendly School

We know that this will be keeping the little ones busy for hours and we are truly happy with this
purchase. Another five star product from Fisher Price.

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Collector 2015 Holiday Doll, Blonde All the Holiday Barbie's are beautiful and make lovely gifts under the Christmas tree, but this 2015 Holiday Barbie is exceptionally beautiful in her old fashioned setting. The Barbie doll herself is blonde with small curls at the bottom, with pale blue eyes and burgundy red lipstick. Her gown is a strapless burgundy bodice with a sheer burgundy ruffled skirt over a silver poinsettia underskirt. The bodice top is trimmed in silver that match both her underskirt and silver drop earrings. Barbie's burgundy gown match her burgundy nail polish and burgundy shoes as well.

The box liner behind the Barbie doll depicts the most beautiful old fashioned Christmas scene from long ago. The scene is in shades of green and white. There is a row of green houses with pine trees and barren trees under the falling snow. In front of the houses is an old fashioned horse drawn sleigh pulling a couple dressed in attire from long ago. On each side of the Barbie doll are clear inserts with beautiful white snow covered barren branches where tiny birds are sitting. These branches and birds frame Barbie beautifully. This elegant Barbie in her silver and burgundy outfit look stunning against the green and white Christmas scene from long ago. When Barbie doll's elegance meet with an old fashioned Christmas, you get a perfect 5 STAR Holiday Barbie.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Collector 2015 Holiday Doll, Blonde

text_fidelity_a:
Gamelyn Games Tiny Epic Dinosaurs,12+ years This took a while for me to review because there just hasn't been a lot of time for Anything lately. I actually thought this was the full sized game. (Also never played but wanted to) So when I got the box and it was barely larger than two boxes of playing cards i went... Well it did say "tiny" on it. I picked up the rules three times and read through them, trying to figure out the solo player game before going "this is not fun to play solo". However we finally sat down and tried out the Tiny Dino game three players. Playing is rather complex involving a small board, cards, and game pieces. It took way longer than the stated 45 minutes, (and TBF we didn't finish all six rounds. Kids quit wanting to play) but that might be because we kept having to figure out order of play, rules and what cards do what. I like the complexity, but it just wasn't a game either of my kids (huge D&D and strategy gamers) liked. They also like rules to be clear, even if complex. So three stars.
One star off because it is hard to read and see in such a small format. One star off because it is needlessly complex, or at least not laid out easily to understand how to play without investing quite a bit of time. Half a star off because one player rules are stupid.
Game free in exchange for an honest review.
text_fidelity_b: Gamelyn Games Tiny Epic Dinosaurs,12+ years

Melissa & Doug Folding Princess Castle Santa brought this princess castle for my 5 year old. She nearly went nuts when she saw it! Both her and her older sister constantly play with it. It's now 3 days after Christmas and they still both love it. Usually after the initial fun wears off (in a few hours) their toys sit unplayed with but not this castle.

It's exactly what you see in the picture. It's big and has lots of rooms, even a dungeon (of sorts) that constantly stir the imagination. Sturdy wood construction, elegantly painted, it's quite a toy. I wish I had one when I was a kid! I also bought the Princess Disney characters others have mentioned instead of the Melissa & Doug characters and they work wonderfully with the castle. I agree that the rooms are small, but I didn't buy this as a doll house for the girls to load up with furniture and pretend it's a real house.....it's a castle with a pretend moat, and dragons and shining knights in armor, and beautiful princesses and evil witches and all those imaginary things which make this castle so much fun to play with!

Also, it's extremely easy to put together. The only things you have to attach are the two towers and the connecting bridge. It arrived very quickly in the mail and was well packaged. I think it's worth the money and I'm about as cheap-minded as they come!

UPDATE: It's July 27, 2009 (7 months after purchase) and the girls both still love this castle. They play with it on an almost daily basis and it's currently set up in their bedroom floor with all sorts of necessary items around and inside of it. It seems to continually stir their imaginations.

Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up I purchased this game while it was on sale, and after playing it for ~20 hours, I would gladly have paid double for the experience. While it is true that it can be a bit intimidating at first for most people, after the initial steep learning curve is over this game really begins to shine. Unlike other legacy games, Gloomhaven is more forgiving in the sense that you don't actually lose anything, but rather you learn from your mistakes and get to try again without penalty.

Even if you don't have other friends who would be willing to play with you, playing by yourself (controlling two characters at once) is incredibly fun and engaging. I would recommend playing with 2 to 3 people though.

My only gripe with the game is that it doesn't include any real solution for organizing the game once you start playing. I would highly recommend Broken Token's Gloomhaven organizer as well as the removable sticker sheet. The BT organizer may be expensive as well, but it's worth every penny.

So, having these pre-sharpened pencils is a great way to start the year.

They are very comfortable to hold, as they don't have the ridges. They are nice and smooth. They feel good in your hands.

The points are very sharp, but don't break easily.

I thought the lead seemed lighter in color than other #2 pencils I've used on my printer paper, but when I used it in my planner it looked like regular #2 lead, so it was probably the paper. If you press down harder, then the color of the lead on the paper looks the same.

It says no latex in eraser. The erasers work better on these pencils than standard pencils which I've used. So, I guess the no latex feature helps.

I find these pencils as good as, or superior, to others I have used.

There would make a great gift for a teacher so she doesn't have to buy pencils out of her personal funds. Or a teacher could give a box to each student at the beginning of the year.

I like the weight and feel of these pencils.

The box which these pencil boxes come in is sturdy, and would fit well in a closet with shelves for storage for the school year.

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Pass The Peas This game has a cute, creative format unlike anything I've seen for a word game. Everything about the game from the container, to the letter trays, and the letters themselves is related to peas. The cardboard trays are made to look like pea pods and the letters look like peas.

The container is a cylinder made of sturdy cardboard in which all the game pieces fit. The letters come in individual, green drawstring bag. If the game was played often, I'm not sure how long the letter trays would hold up, but other than that, everything does seem fairly durable.

Unfortunately, the game itself doesn't live up to the clever concept. Each player draws 10 letters from their bag of letters and has 30 seconds to make a word. Then all players "pass the peas" to the next player, who tries to use as many of their own letters to make a new word out of the original word passed to them. The only requirement is at least one of the original letters must be left remaining. For example, you can add an "S" to the beginning and an "S" to the end to make the word "TOP" into a new word "STOPS" or you can change "DUST" into "LINT" by replacing the "DUS" with "LIN".

The game sounds like it could be fun, but it is frustrating. I play online word games often, but still found it hard to think of a word using my letters and get them arranged on the tray within 30 seconds. It was also hard to make a new word when one of your opponent's trays was passed to you. I first played the game with just one other player and thought maybe adding another player would make the game more fun, but the main problem was the difficulty in making words and not the pace of the game, it wasn't any better with three players. After repeated games full of frustration, it became boring and nobody wanted to play any longer, which is a shame since the pea theme is so clever. An elementary school child might have fun ignoring the timer and the rules and just using the letters to make words since the game pieces are so cute.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Pass The Peas

text_fidelity_a:
Magnatab — A to Z Uppercase — Activity for Fun and Learning — Sensory Activity — Ages 3+ SUMMARY
This is a fun and clever toy that can really help kids learn their letters. It certainly captures their attention initially but after 2 days it doesn't seem to be interesting any more. For longer term interest I would suggest the Magnatab that is more of a doodle pad. It is a durable toy and looks like it would stand up in a classroom. However, the magnetic stylus is not attached to the rest of the toy and could very easily be lost.

FULL REVIEW

KIDS COMMENTS
My kids want you to know that they like the sound that the beads make when they pop up and they like how the beads "appear" when they put the magnet to them.

FORM - A+
This toy is nicely sized. It perfectly fits in an adult or child's lap and has a nice curved edge around the back that makes it nice to hold. The letters are nicely sized and spaced on the board. The stylus is comfortable in the hand and easy for little fingers to hold without being bulky. The slot that the stylus fits into for storage is super clever and has a magnet that holds it in place. In concept and usage I like this better than a stylus attached with a string or plastic loop. However, practically, I'm afraid that the stylus will be lost since it is not attached to the rest of the toy.

DURABILITY - A-
I immediately gave this toy to 4 children, ages 7-18 months. They loved it for the first two days. It got tossed, sat on, fought over, and played with pretty constantly. The only problem that I saw was some faint smudging of the black print on the Magnatab. It looks like some excess toner being wiped or smudged across the surface. However, none of the print has come off yet and the direction arrows are still nice and dark. I believe this toy is durable enough to stand up in an education environment. Other than the stylus issues described above this toy would be a good investment for a school or day care.
text_fidelity_b: Magnatab — A to Z Uppercase — Activity for Fun and Learning — Sensory Activity — Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Sticker & Chill — Flower Fest — Relax and Unwind with Repositionable Stickers — Adults This set comes with 10 different backgrounds with corresponding pages of cling stickers, all spiral bound.There are scenes from the 1950s, 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s.The details for each decade are really cute, such as a boombox and cassette tapes for the 80s, a green and orange background for a 70s rec room with lava lamps and throw pillows in those colors, peace signs and daisies to decorate a 60s van, and full skirts, hats, and gloves for 50s fashions. All were fun, but my favorites were the fifties scenes.

Many of the smaller stickers are a little hard to peel off, but the larger ones are easy to peel off. They stick well onto the scenes as long as you don’t try to place one completely over another sticker. (Like putting a bow over a skirt.) They are easy to pull up and reposition or remove from the scene. It’s easier than I expected to put the cling stickers back where they came from for storage, but if you’re putting a large number of them away, it’s hard to tell where on the sheet the stickers were originally. I’ve just been storing most of them in the scenes I’ve placed them and they have stayed in place well. This has been a fun alternative to coloring pages. I really recommend this as a fun way to relax while listening to music or watching television.
text_fidelity_b: Sticker & Chill — Flower Fest — Relax and Unwind with Repositionable Stickers — Adults
